key_insight: Fatigue performance in thick-wall pressure-vessel welds depends on the coupled effects of welding-induced microstructure, local mechanical mismatch, and residual stress.
engineering_relevance: Welding and post-weld heat-treatment choices should jointly manage microstructural heterogeneity and residual stress to improve fatigue resistance.
method: Review arc, narrow-gap, electron-beam, and laser welding as distinct thermal-history generators.
Synthesize microstructure evolution, residual-stress development, and fatigue mechanisms in SA508 and Cr-Mo-V steels.
Assess spatially resolved characterization and thermometallurgical-mechanical modelling approaches.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a critical literature review supported by characterization and modelling methods, but reports no quantitative fatigue results or comparative benchmarks.
watch_item: Post-weld heat treatment redistributes stress while changing phases and precipitates, so fatigue benefits require validation for the specific joint and service environment.
paper_title: Microstructural Evolution and Fatigue Performance of Welded Joints in Thick-Wall Pressure Vessels
